newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bumper earnings tipped for Hong Kong banks.
newsitem.headline: Bumper earnings tipped for Hong Kong banks.

text.p: Hong Kong investors are gearing up for bumper 1996 earnings reports from the territory's banks, sending bank shares soaring this week and pushing shares of HSBC Holdings Plc to record highs, analysts said on Thursday.
"The banks are in favour because people are confident about upcoming earnings results," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"There is a bit of optimism on the current performance and the idea that the banks will grow their earnings in 1997."
Analysts said they expected earnings growth at the big banks in Hong Kong to top 15 percent for 1996.

Market heavyweight HSBC Holdings, which is due to report its 1996 results on March 3, is expected to post a rise of more than 20 percent. Its share price traded at an all-time high of HK$181.00 ($23.40) in Thursday's morning session, up HK$2.00, after surging HK$8.50 on Wednesday.
Andrew Brown, head of financial institutions research for Asia at Salomon Brothers, forecast 1996 earnings per share of HK$14.30 compared with HK$11.47 in 1995, for HSBC.
"There were some one-time gains in the early part of 1996 in addition to a strong overall performance of various banking units, especially strong performance in Asia," he said.
HSBC Holdings reported attributable profit for the six months to June 30, 1996 of HK$18.74 billion or HK$7.11 a share.
Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, forecast 1996 earnings per share of HK$14.10 and net profit of HK$37.4 billion versus 1995's HK$30.04 billion.

"Recurrent earnings are expected to grow 19 percent. Basically Asia has grown fairly strongly," he said. For HSBC subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd, Hutcheson said he was expecting an earnings per share rise of 20 percent. Hang Seng Bank posted 1995 earnings per share of HK$4.13.
It had net profit for the six months ended June 30, 1996, of HK$4.35 billion and earnings per share of HK$2.25.

"Hang Seng Bank earnings will be driven by a confluence of factors," said Brown. "Dramatic expansion in net interest margin compared with 1995 combined with strong loan growth should produce a very attractive net interest income growth which is the preponderance of revenue at the bank."
He expected 1996 earnings per share of HK$4.90.
Brown said the bank should also benefit from strong control of expense growth, attractive fee-related revenue growth and possibly higher gains on the sale of securities.

"We also expect Bank of East Asia to produce attractive core earnings growth," he said, adding that he expected 23 percent growth at the core earnings level. Bank of East Asia Ltd reported 1995 net profit of HK$1.64 billion.
Hang Seng Bank shares slipped HK$0.25 to close at HK$96.00 at midday on Thursday after rising HK$2.75 on Wednesday. Bank of East Asia was steady at HK$37.30 after Wednesday's HK$1.30 jump.
Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities, said HSBC shares still looked "seriously undervalued".
"We are looking at about HK$196 (a share) by the time they announce results," he said, adding that he expected net profit of HK$36.5 billion and earnings per share growth of 20 percent.
But Brown said the recent rise in Hong Kong banking shares looked stretched and a correction may set in before the results.

"We see the very recent sharp run up as a little stretched for the near term and very similar to the past two results announcement trading patterns of the bank stocks, being a mentality of buying on expectations and selling on results."

But Brown said he remained positive on the sector. "We have and continue to remain bullish on the banking sector in Hong Kong. We do expect results to be good for 1996 and we are bullish on the whole sector for 1997," he said.
-- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6345 ($1= HK$7.74)
